Anomalies on isopycnals, against a baseline on the same surfaces

Source: R/isopycnal.R
cc_isopycnal_anomaly.Rd

cc_isopycnal() for the casts asked for, beside a baseline built the way the release builds its climatology (calcofi4db::build_climatology()), but on density surfaces instead of 10 m depth bins: for each station (site_key), the cruise's month (or its season, season = TRUE: DJF / MAM / JJA / SON), each surface and each variable, the mean over the casts of cruises in years, kept where at least min_cruises distinct cruises contribute. anomaly = value - clim_mean; a cast with no baseline cell comes back NA, never 0. For variable = "depth_m" the anomaly is the surface's displacement in metres, positive deeper.

Usage

cc_isopycnal_anomaly(
  con,
  sigma = c(seq(24, 27, by = 0.2), 25.5, 26.5),
  cruise_key = NULL,
  site_key = NULL,
  variables = c("temperature_ave", "salinity_ave_corr", "oxygen_ml_l_ave_sta_corr",
    "est_nitrate_sta_corr", "spiciness0"),
  years = c(1993, 2013),
  season = FALSE,
  min_cruises = 5,
  direction = c("down", "both"),
  surface_max_m = 20,
  min_n = 3,
  baseline = c("auto", "release", "compute")
)

Arguments

con

DuckDB connection to a release opened with the supplemental tables: cc_get_db(supplemental = TRUE).

sigma

numeric: the surfaces, sigma-theta in kg m^-3. The default is the provider's list (Rasmus Swalethorp, 2026-11-13): 24.0 to 27.0 by 0.2, plus 25.5 and 26.5, which sit near the cores of the California Current and the California Undercurrent. 27.0 is reached by about a quarter of the down casts (the median density at the bottom of a 500 m cast is 26.98).

cruise_key

optional cruise key(s) (YYYY-MM-NODC) to restrict to.

site_key

optional station(s) (sample.site_key, e.g. "093.3 030.0").

variables

obs_ctd_full measurement types to carry onto each surface, and "spiciness0" for spice computed there (see the rules); the default is the sensor-pair averages the release publishes (the station-corrected oxygen and the bottle-fitted nitrate estimate, which exist only on casts with bottle data) and spice.

years

two-element baseline range of cruise years, inclusive (default 1993-2013, the release's window).

season

FALSE (default) for the monthly baseline; TRUE for the seasonal one.

min_cruises

minimum distinct cruises behind a baseline cell (the release keeps >= 5).

direction

"down" (default): one cast per station occupation, the down cast where there is one; "both": every cast.

surface_max_m, min_n

as in calcofi4db::profile_threshold_depth(): the deepest first bin that counts as the surface (m) and the fewest bins a cast needs for "at_surface".

baseline

"auto" (default): the release's climatology when it carries this baseline, computed otherwise; "release": the release's, an error when it does not carry it; "compute": always computed from obs_ctd_full.

Value

cc_isopycnal()'s columns plus clim_mean, clim_sd, clim_n (casts), n_cruises, anomaly, anomaly_sd; attributes baseline (the years), period ("month" or "season"), source ("release" or "computed") and climatology (the baseline cells: site_key, month, sigma_theta, variable, clim_mean, clim_sd, clim_n, n_cruises).

Details

Where the baseline comes from. A release from v2026.11.14 on carries the baseline on these surfaces in its climatology table (calcofi4db::build_climatology(isopycnal_tbl = ), built from the release's isopycnal table: the cells with a sigma_theta, types cc_isopycnal_type()), and that is what is subtracted (baseline = "auto") whenever it is the baseline asked for: the release's window (years), down casts and the default surface_max_m / min_n, every surface in sigma and every variable in variables present. Only the casts asked for are then computed. Otherwise (an older release, another window, direction = "both", a surface the release does not carry) the baseline is computed here from obs_ctd_full at the stations of the casts asked for, reading every cruise of the window at those stations, by the same rules. The release keeps cells with at least 5 cruises, so a min_cruises below 5 still finds only those there, as cc_climatology() does. The two give the same anomalies (to the release's rounding of the mean, 1e-6); attr(, "source") says which was used.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
con <- cc_get_db(supplemental = TRUE)
an  <- cc_isopycnal_anomaly(con, sigma = seq(24.4, 26.6, by = 0.2),
                            cruise_key = "2026-11-33P4", season = TRUE)
# the displacement of each surface and the temperature change on it, station by station
dplyr::filter(an, variable %in% c("depth_m", "temperature_ave"))
} # }
